'''Paul Busch''' (15 February 1955 – 9 June 2018) was a German-born mathematical physicist, known for his work in [[quantum mechanics]]. He made pioneering contributions to [[quantum measurement theory]], being an advocate of the use of [[POVM]]s, and to the [[uncertainty principle]] in quantum mechanics, where he developed a mathematical formulation of a measurement-disturbance relation.<ref>Paul Busch, Pekka Lahti, and Reinhard F. Werner "Proof of Heisenberg's Error-Disturbance Relation" Phys. Rev. Lett. 111, 160405 [https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.111.160405 DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.111.160405]</ref>

He was a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Hull]] and the [[University of York]]. He published over 100 scientific articles<ref>R.Colbeck, L. Loveridge and S. Weigert "Paul Busch: Contributions to Quantum Theory", Journal of Physics: Conference Series, Vol. 1638, Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Mechanics – in memoriam Paul Busch. [https://doi.org/10.1088/1742-6596/1638/1/012014 DOI:10.1088/1742-6596/1638/1/012014]</ref> and co-authored three books: ''The Quantum Theory of Measurement'',<ref>P. Busch, P. Lahti, P. Mittelstaedt "The Quantum Theory of Measurement", Lecture Notes in Physics, Vol. m2, Springer-Verlag, Berlin, 1991. Second revised edition 1996. [https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-37205-9 DOI: 10.1007/978-3-540-37205-9]</ref> ''Operational Quantum Physics''<ref>P. Busch, M. Grabowski, P. Lahti "Operational Quantum Physics", Lecture Notes in Physics, Vol. m31, Springer-Verlag, Berlin, 1995. Second, corrected printing 1997. [https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-49239-9 DOI: 10.1007/978-3-540-49239-9]</ref> and ''Quantum Measurement''.<ref>P. Busch, P. Lahti, J.-P. Pellonpää, K. Ylinen "Quantum Measurement", Theoretical and Mathematical Physics, Springer International Publishing, 2016. [https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-43389-9 DOI:10.1007/978-3-319-43389-9]</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Busch was born in Refrath, a district of [[Bergisch Gladbach]], Germany in February 1955. He studied at the [[University of Cologne]], obtaining a Diploma in Physics in 1979 and a Ph.D. in 1982 under the supervision of [[Peter Mittelstaedt]]. The title of his Ph.D. thesis was ''Indeterminacy relations and simultaneous measurements in quantum theory''. He followed his PhD with a [[Habilitation]] in Mathematical Physics from the University of Cologne, for a thesis entitled ''Physical aspects of a generalised observable concept in quantum theory''.<ref name="obituary" />

==Career==
Busch held positions at [[Florida Atlantic University]] (1986), the [[Max Planck Institute for Biophysical Chemistry|Max Planck Institute (Göttingen)]] (1987–88), and the [[University of Heidelberg]] (1994).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://c222b2d2-fac1-4518-b22e-974ade22aba0.filesusr.com/ugd/7a65e4_4731c5d2efa440a588c682dc53724221.pdf |title=Curriculum vitae: Paul Busch FInstP |date=January 2018 |access-date=13 December 2020 }}</ref> In 1995, he moved to the [[University of Hull]], where he was successively lecturer, reader and professor of mathematical physics; he was head of the department of mathematics from 2001 to 2005. He joined the [[University of York]] as professor of mathematics in 2005, where he remained until his death. He was additionally an adjunct professor of theoretical physics at the [[University of Turku]] in Finland (from 1991), and also held visiting professorships at the [[Lyman Laboratory of Physics]], [[Harvard University]] (1994–95) and the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]] in [[Waterloo, Ontario]] (2005–07).<ref name="obituary" />

He died in June 2018 after a short illness.<ref name="obituary">{{Cite journal|last1=Gudder|first1=Stan|last2=Lahti|first2=Pekka|last3=Loveridge|first3=Leon|date=September 2018|title=Paul Busch 1955–2018|journal=Foundations of Physics|language=en|volume=48|issue=9|pages=1128–1130|doi=10.1007/s10701-018-0206-8|bibcode=2018FoPh...48.1128G|s2cid=125657332|issn=0015-9018|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Honours ==
Busch was elected a Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]] in 2014 and a full member of L'Académie Internationale de Philosophie des Sciences in 2016.<ref name="obituary"/> He was President of the International Quantum Structures Association (2016 until his death).<ref name="obituary" />
